issues.title: [CI Failure]: Recurring flaky infrastructure failures — AMD GPU hangs, H200-MIG step timeouts, agent loss (200-build analysis)
issues.author: khluu
issues.body_head:
## Summary

An analysis of the last **200 builds** of the `ci` pipeline (builds 89402–89599, all branches) found **240 jobs that failed on their first attempt and then passed on retry** — i.e. flaky. Reading each failing attempt's log shows the flakiness is **~78% infrastructure/environment**, not vLLM code. This issue tracks the three dominant, recurring infrastructure causes so they can be triaged to fleet/runner owners.

Method: enumerated builds via the Buildkite API, listed each build's jobs from the public `/data/jobs` endpoint, selected jobs where the original attempt had `passed=false` and the `retried_in_job_uuid` replacement had `passed=true`, then fetched and read each failing attempt's log.

## Root-cause distribution (240 flaky instances)

| Category | Count | % | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Step timeout (cancelled while passing) | 74 | 31% | Config/tuning |
| Crash — AMD GPU HW fault | 57 | 24% | Hardware/driver |
| Buildkite agent lost (empty log, exit -1) | 53 | 22% | Runner infra |
| Docker build/pull EOF / registry | 19 | 8% | Infra |
| Test assertion (genuinely flaky test) | 14 | 6% | Test code |
| Network (HF/crates/github download) | 8 | 3% | Infra |
| GPU free-memory < desired utilization | 6 | 2.5% | Runner hygiene |
| Other (git-mirror checkout lock, etc.) | 7 | 3% | Infra |
| Race/deadlock | 2 | 1% | — |

## 1. AMD GPU hardware/driver hangs — ~44 instances (top specific cause)

Logs show `HW Exception by GPU node-2 … reason: GPU Hang` → `Fatal Python error: Aborted` (SIGABRT / exit 134), plus a few `Memory access fault … write to read-only page` and SRAM/DRAM ECC failures. These hit many different AMD test jobs indiscriminately and clear on retry (the retry lands on a healthy GPU). This is a transient MI300/MI250 hardware / ROCm-driver issue, not a vLLM bug.

Representative jobs: `:amd: (MI300) Basic Models (Other)`, `:amd: (MI300) Entrypoints Integration (OpenAI API chat_completion)`, `:amd: (MI300) V1 Spec Decode`, `:amd: (MI300) Multimodal Models (Standard) 4`.

**Ask:** fleet-health / GPU-reset handling on the AMD runners; consider auto-cordoning nodes that raise repeated GPU Hang / ECC events.

## 2. NVIDIA H200-MIG step timeouts — ~59 instances

Jobs are cancelled (`Received cancellation signal`, exit -1, `timed_out=True`) while tests are still *passing*. Concentrated in spec-decode and multimodal suites on the slower MIG slices:

- `:nvidia: (H200 MIG 18GB) Spec Decode Draft Model` (10×)
- `:nvidia: (H200 MIG 18GB) Multimodal Processor` (7×)
- `:nvidia: (H200 MIG 35GB) Spec Decode N-Gram + Suffix` (7×)

Root causes visible in logs: slow Triton/JIT kernel warmup (one log showed 121 compile keys at ~57 s/key), repeated `EngineCore` startup per test, and long GSM8K/lm-eval runs. Several jobs had all tests pass but exceeded the step timeout in teardown.

**Ask:** bump `timeout_in_minutes` (or shard further) for these suites on MIG hardware. This is data-backed tuning; happy to open a PR if a target timeout is agreed.

## 3. Buildkite agent loss — 53 instances (all NVIDIA/L4)

Empty 0-byte logs, `started_at: null`, exit -1: the runner agent died or never accepted the job, then a fresh agent passed on retry. Concentrated on the L4 NixlConnector / Pipeline+Context-Parallel distributed jobs.

**Ask:** investigate L4 runner stability.

## Already addressed

- The dominant *test-code* flake, `test_sharded_sampling_outputs_match` on AMD (11×), is fixed by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57369.
- The GPU free-memory flake already has a draft PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57362.

## Environment

Observed on `main` across builds 89402–89599 (2026-09-17).

---

🤖 This analysis was performed with AI assistance (Kimi Code); each classification was derived from reading the actual failing-attempt Buildkite log.

issues.title: [CI Failure]: Multimodal Processor shards - test_tensor_schema[naver-hyperclovax/HyperCLOVAX-SEED-Think-32B] - upstream model_type hyperclovax_vision_v2 unknown to CI transformers
issues.author: kaijunli-infr
issues.body_head:
### Name of failing test

`models/multimodal/processing/test_tensor_schema.py::test_model_tensor_schema[naver-hyperclovax/HyperCLOVAX-SEED-Think-32B]`

### Basic information

- Jobs: every `Multimodal Processor` shard containing this model — observed on `computer-cpu-multimodal-processor-shard-2`, `shard-4`, `nvidia-h200-mig-18gb-multimodal-processor`, and `amd-mi355-multimodal-processor` in build 88212 (PR #52101, which does not touch multimodal code).
- Deterministic, hardware-independent, and survives retries: the cause is external to the repo.

### Description

The upstream Hugging Face repo changed its `model_type` to `hyperclovax_vision_v2`, which the transformers version in the CI images does not recognize, so `ModelConfig` validation fails:

```text
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for ModelConfig
  Value error, The checkpoint you are trying to load has model type `hyperclovax_vision_v2` but Transformers does not recognize this architecture.
```

153/154 tests in each shard pass; only this model fails.

### Possible fixes

Pin the test to a fixed revision of the HF repo, update/upgrade transformers in the CI image, or temporarily skip this model id in `test_tensor_schema`.
